text:
maria: Anyone else seeing a pileup of tiny GPU pods in ap-southeast1 pending? Started ~10:03 UTC, +80 small pods in Pending with no obvious node alloc.
ken: Yep, spikes in the pending queue and a weird taint churn alert. My dashboard shows warm-node pool dropping available slots.
sam: I see lots of `NodeAffinity` small-pod requests that are getting matched then immediately evicted. Logs show `taint:gpu-hot=true:NoSchedule` flips around the same time.
anya: Could be the network egress throttle we had last night causing the warm-node sync to fail and lose the lease? That would orphan pods on warm nodes.
maria: ops-bot posted this alert: `ALERT: small_pod_pending_rate > 15/min across ap-southeast1` with a stacktrace pointing at scheduler reconciliation timeouts.
scheduler-bot: reconciliation latency moved from 120ms -> 2.4s between 10:02 and 10:08. Requeue counts x4.
lee: Reproduced locally: when the warm pool controller fails to refresh leases, nodes toggle a transient taint `warm-stale=true:NoExecute` and scheduler prefers other racks -> churn.
ken: Is this the same as last month's 'ghost pod' pattern or a new variant? Last time it was nvlink probes failing.
sam: Different symptoms. That one was nvlink heat. This looks like lease refresh / conntrack errors upstream. I pulled kube-scheduler logs, snippet: ```
I0403 10:05:21.123 scheduler.go:452] failed predicate for pod small-123: node(s) had taint warm-stale:NoExecute
I0403 10:05:22.456 scheduler.go:478] requeue pod small-123, attempt=3 reason=ReconcileTimeout
```
anya: Also seeing a flood of `AttachVolume` RPC timeouts in the same window. Could be control-plane egress flapping to the storage/kv service.
lee: Quick mitigation idea: lower warm-pool eviction sensitivity and add a short backoff before applying `NoExecute` taint so scheduler has time to place. That would reduce immediate churn.
ken: We should be careful: lowering sensitivity may hold unhealthy nodes longer and increase failed jobs. Maybe only apply for pods with `priorityClass=system-medium` and keep preempt thresholds.
maria: For a fast rollback: can we change the warm-pool controller to stop re-tainting nodes for 5 minutes in ap-southeast1?
sam: I can push a scoped patch: `controlplane/warmpool: add env SKIP_RETAINT_REGION=ap-southeast1` — small feature flag to stop reapplying taints. Will deploy to canary within 5 min.
ops-bot: deploy request created by sam: PR #4821 -> canary ap-southeast1. ETA 6m. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
anya: While that's rolling, can infra-tooling run a one-off `kubectl patch` to set `warm-stale:NoExecute` -> `warm-stale:NoSchedule`? That would avoid evicting existing pods but still prevent scheduling new ones on nodes.
lee: Good call. That buys time and keeps currently running pods alive.
ken: Post-mitigation followups: need a root cause check for the egress control-plane incidents to KV service (timestamps 10:00-10:12). Add a postmortem if the patch goes to prod.
maria: Agreed. Also let's capture a sample pod flow for later: ```
kubectl describe pod small-123 -n ml-jobs
Events:
  10:02:01  Scheduled  Successfully assigned ml-node-17
  10:05:21  TaintAdded  node/ml-node-17: warm-stale:NoExecute
  10:05:21  Evicted     The node was marked for eviction
  10:06:10  Failed      pod couldn't attach gpu-device: rpc error timeout
```
sam: Canary went green in ap-southeast1 canary cluster. Patch reverted tainting for the region. Pending queue dropped from 80 -> 6 in ~4 minutes.
maria: Nice. Leave the canary for 30m and then roll to primary if telemetry stable.
ken: Post-action items: (1) increase observability on warmpool lease refresh latency, (2) add a heuristic to delay NoExecute taints for <2m, (3) run an egress connectivity drill for control-plane KV endpoints.
anya: I'll own #1 and #3. Sam, can you do #2?
sam: Yup, will draft RFC and a small change for the controller.
lee: Thanks all — saving this thread for the postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
